decisionsTitle: The terms say the club may refuse or cancel a registration, on objective grounds only (amending §418)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01**, on the race's first day of registrations: «Pe viitor trebuie să spunem că ne rezervăm dreptul de a accepta sau refuza un participant, să evităm situații de genul». The dispatcher's brief gave the sentence for the terms: «Organizatorul nu refuză și nu anulează o înscriere pe niciun criteriu interzis de lege.»

**What the terms in force say today.** No general sentence about the club refusing a registration. Three narrow ones: §4 «o înscriere cu o dată a nașterii care arată mai puțin este refuzată» (the minimum age), §4's stopping or excluding on the course («poate fi oprit sau exclus pe loc, fără despăgubire»), and §8 «Clubul poate anula o astfel de înscriere, refuza înscrierile viitoare ale persoanei și limita temporar accesul la platformă» (automated registrations, somebody else's data, a false identity document). Nothing names the grounds together, nothing says the person is told why, and nothing says what happens to the place.

**Decision.**

1. **The terms' template says it, in §3 «Anularea» / "Cancelling", as its last paragraph, in both languages.** «Clubul poate refuza o înscriere sau o poate anula după ce a fost făcută doar pe un motiv obiectiv:» — the event's participation conditions not met (the minimum age, the declarations it asks for, the statement of medical fitness where the event asks it); false, incomplete or another person's data; the event's capacity or safety (the weather, the course, the number of volunteers); conduct contrary to the event's rules or dangerous to others; a registration made against these terms. «Îți spunem motivul pe e-mail — sau pe ecran, când chiar formularul refuză înscrierea —, iar locul eliberat, când este cazul, trece la lista de așteptare, după regulile obișnuite.» (the «când este cazul» because a refusal on the capacity ground frees no place) (the allocator of §104 and §587; nothing new). «La un eveniment gratuit nu este nimic de restituit; dacă ai plătit clubului o taxă de participare, se aplică regulile de restituire de mai sus.» And last: «Clubul nu refuză și nu anulează o înscriere pe niciun criteriu interzis de lege.» / "The club refuses or cancels no registration on any ground the law forbids." The sentence says «Clubul» where the brief said «Organizatorul»: the terms name their party «clubul» (§1), and on another organiser's event the club is not the organiser, so «Organizatorul» would be a word the text never defines. No article number in the paragraph, no club fact, no merge field.
2. **Why §3, not a new section.** Cancelling a registration already made is the club ending the agreement on its own, which Codul civil art. 1203 lets a standard clause do only when it is accepted expressly. §3 is already among the clauses §1 says are accepted by the form's separate box, so §1's list now reads «3 (anularea înscrierii sau a evenimentului ori modificarea evenimentului)» / "3 (cancelling a registration or an event, or changing an event)". The sections keep their numbers, so no cross-reference moves. **The form's box keeps the words the legal review fixed (§425)**: «…clauzele despre anularea sau modificarea evenimentului de către club, …». Whether it must also name the cancelling of a registration is the lawyer's question, not a change made here; CLAUDE.md «Still owed» item 16 asks it.
3. **The declarations: nothing added.** The four declaration templates were read for any sentence about the organiser refusing or cancelling. They say the organiser may change, shorten, stop or cancel the event for safety, and may refuse the start only for missing mandatory equipment. Neither contradicts the terms: both are about the event and the start line, not about refusing a registration. The right to refuse belongs in the terms; the declarations stay the participant's own statements.
4. **The app says the same.** A staff cancellation had no reason kinds: one free-text reason, kept in the audit row and never sent to the person, whose email said only «a fost anulată». The participant's own reasons (§558: injury, other plans, another reason) are the person's, not the club's. So the registration's page in the backoffice gains one box under the cancel form: «Clubul refuză înscrierea, potrivit termenilor: motivul scris mai sus îi este trimis persoanei pe e-mail», with a caption under 200 characters (§511): «Doar pe un motiv obiectiv din termeni: condiții neîndeplinite, date false, capacitate sau siguranță, conduită. Niciodată pe un criteriu interzis de lege. Nebifat, motivul rămâne doar în jurnal.» Ticked, the same verb runs (`cancelRegistrationByStaff`, `kind: "REFUSED_BY_ORGANIZER"`): the same state check, the same allocator releasing the place to the front of the waiting list, Administrator-only as every cancel (§67), asserted in the service. The reason the Administrator typed is the ground. It is written into the cancellation email's payload (never onto the row), and the email gains, before «Locul a fost eliberat.», «Clubul a refuzat această înscriere. Motivul: „…”.» / "The club refused this registration. The ground: “…”." It also links «Termenii și condițiile» in each half's language, from `APP_BASE_URL`. The email says nothing about what the terms allow and names no section number: the terms in force may be a version without the new paragraph or with other sections, and a sentence describing them would then misstate the document it links. The audit row keeps who and why as today, with `kind: "REFUSED_BY_ORGANIZER"` beside the reason. A refusal with an empty ground is refused (`VALIDATION_ERROR` on the reason). The row menu's and bulk cancel's help says a refusal under the terms is made from the registration's own page, where its ground is emailed (`bulkCancelHelp`). The list's row menu and the bulk cancel post no box and stay ordinary cancellations: a refusal is one person's, with its own ground. No migration, no new verb, no new enum value.
5. **`/admin/tasks`: nothing new.** Its notice rows (`listStatesNotice`, `promoNotice`, `sponsorNotice`, …) each detect one merge field in the notice in force. A paragraph of plain text in the terms has no marker to detect, and «the terms' template moved after the version in force» is already what `/admin/legal` shows as «Șablon nou» (§532), by the template's hash. CLAUDE.md «Still owed» item 16 gains one sentence instead (the approval, and the box's words).

**What changes on the sites.** The texts in force keep their words and their hashes until the club approves the terms from the new template in `/admin/legal`. The staff box works today. Until then its email states only the fact and the ground and links the terms, and the terms in force only cover a refusal through §4's age rule and §8's misuse rule; the email asserts nothing the terms in force do not say.

**A Romanian lawyer reads this paragraph first** (§3's last), as §568's risks paragraph. These notes are the platform's reading of the Civil Code, not legal advice.

*Rejected:* the owner's own wording as a bare, unconditional reservation, «ne rezervăm dreptul de a accepta sau refuza un participant». It protects the club less than the terms with grounds: a right with no stated ground is the one a court reads against the party who wrote the clause (Codul civil art. 1203 and the rule on unfair terms), and it is the very situation the owner wants to avoid, a refusal nobody can explain. So the terms keep his intent, the right to refuse or cancel, and give it the objective grounds and the duty to tell the ground. A per-event setting: the right is the same for every event. Refusing silently: the person must be told. A separate staff verb «Refuză»: the same transition as a cancel, and §67 allows no new verb. A list of grounds to pick from on the staff form: the terms' grounds are broad categories, and the person is owed the concrete fact, which only the typed reason carries.

Amends §418. Tests: unit `tests/unit/legal-documents/terms-refusal.test.ts` (new); the terms' length ceiling in `merge-fields.test.ts` moved from 11000 to 12000; integration `tests/integration/registrations/staff-crud.test.ts` (the refusal's email, place and audit row; a refusal without a ground; an ordinary cancel's email carries no reason).
changelogLine: - **The terms say the club may refuse or cancel a registration** — on objective grounds only (conditions not met, false data, capacity or safety, conduct), told by email with the ground, never on a ground the law forbids; the club approves the terms from the new template in /admin/legal. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the platform's terms template, then it states that the organizer may refuse or cancel a registration only on the objective grounds it lists, that the person is told by email with the ground and the place released by the ordinary rules, and that no registration is refused on a ground the law forbids, in both languages; the texts in force are unchanged until the club approves a new version (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an Administrator cancelling a registration from its page with «Clubul refuză înscrierea, potrivit termenilor» ticked, then the same cancellation runs — the place released to the front of the waiting list through the allocator, Administrator-only — and the person's cancellation email says, in both languages, that the club refused the registration under the terms, quotes the reason typed as the ground and links the terms; the audit row records the actor, the reason and `kind: REFUSED_BY_ORGANIZER`; a refusal with no ground is refused; unticked, the reason never reaches the person (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
